text.p: British world champion Jonathan Edwards on Friday offered to coach youngsters in Sarajevo but U.S. sprinter Dennis Mitchell said he would not compete in the war-torn city because it was too dangerous.

Edwards, triple jump world champion and world record holder, wants to make up for missing the International Amateur Athletic Federation's solidarity meeting in Sarajevo on Monday because of a long-standing sponsorship engagement on the same day.
But U.S. champion Mitchell, like Edwards in Milan for Saturday's IAAF Grand Prix final, insisted: "Although track and field is my life, it's not worth my life.
"I don't believe it is safe enough for me to go there and a few other athletes feel the same way.
"I would like to one day but I have talked this over with my family and, as a group, we have decided it would not be good for me to run."
Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson is also unlikely to join the IAAF airlift from Milan.

But top distance runners Noureddine Morceli and Daniel Komen have pledged their support, while Edwards is prepared to hold coaching clinics at a later date despite being embarrassed by the world governing body.
The IAAF used him to promote the meeting in a press release headed "Jonathan Edwards appeals to world stars -- join me in Sarajevo".
It quotes him as saying: "I understand the concerns of some of my colleagues...just nine months after the ceasefire was signed.
"But what type of character do we show by going to the Grand Prix final, where there is a lot of money to make, but refusing to make the trip to Sarajevo as a humanitarian gesture?"
Edwards, Atlanta Olympic silver medallist, said on Friday: "This doesn't seem an ideal way to carry on. It's a bit embarrassing.
"I always stated in principle I would like to compete but there was certainly no definite agreement from me.

"There was no triple jump on the programme until three weeks ago, while I have had an agreement with a sponsor for several months. I'm disappointed it has happened like this. Maybe wires have become crossed.
"Hopefully, it can be worked out that I do some coaching there after the season ends and that will make up for it."
